---
title: "Harness over model — Mark Kashef on Nate Herk (video breakdown + gap analysis)"
date: 2026-09-12
type: video-note
source: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6LNlCpQPYFc
video_title: "How to Actually Choose the Right AI Agent"
channel: Nate Herk | AI Automation
guest: Mark Kashef (Prompt Advisors)
published: 2026-09-11
duration: 34:08
tags: [ai-harness, claude-code, codex, pi, skills, aios, context-engineering]
---

# Harness over model

Video: **"How to Actually Choose the Right AI Agent"** — Nate Herk with **Mark Kashef**, 34 min, posted 2026-09-11.

## The one idea

> "The harness of a model is much more important than the model itself." — Kashef, 0:06

The model is a **brain in a jar**. It takes input, gives output. That is all.
Everything that makes it useful — read, write, edit, bash, grep, the agentic loop —
is the **harness** wrapped around it.

At 2:20 the whiteboard shows this literally: a detailed factory drawing with a glowing
brain in a jar at the dead centre, surrounded by machinery (books = read, press = write,
gears = bash, robot arms = tools). Two boxes at the bottom are crossed out — the things
a bare brain cannot do.

**Proof demo (7:19–8:55):** Kashef opens LM Studio with a local Qwen model (captions read
"Quen 27B" — likely a 7B-class Qwen, too small on screen to confirm) — a raw brain with no
harness — and asks it to build a landing page *and spin up a local server*.
It writes the HTML. It cannot start the server. No limbs.
Give the same prompt to Claude Code or Codex and it does not blink.

**The workflow prediction that follows (3:25–3:41):** open-source local models already do
"like 80% of the day-to-day work." He expects a world within a year where you run
**70–80% locally** (given the hardware) and only "bring in the geniuses for genius-level
tasks or planning." The harness is what makes that split possible — the local brain gets
the same limbs as the expensive one.

**The consequence for benchmarks (20:29–21:45):** after the March 2026 Claude Code harness
leak, Kashef read the whole thing. Most of it was *crutches* — regex lists of swear words,
behaviour guards, scaffolding. His takeaway:

> "There is a whole factory of workers making this model look way smarter than it is."

So stop being impressed by benchmark scores. Ask instead how well the provider improved
**the harness** to match the new brain. Judge empirically, on your own tasks.

---

## Chapter map

| Time | Topic |
|---|---|
| 0:00 | Intro |
| 2:05 | Models vs. harnesses (the brain-in-a-jar diagram) |
| 7:19 | Local models in LM Studio — the no-harness proof |
| 9:26 | Sponsor (skip) |
| 10:29 | Choosing and switching AI agents |
| 13:37 | Hermes, OpenClaw, and **Pi** |
| 16:47 | Making your skills portable (`/poly-skill`) |
| 19:17 | Understanding your AI system |
| 21:46 | Keeping your AI OS updated (`rot.md`) |
| 24:14 | When models outgrow your skills |
| 30:01 | Organizing projects and global rules (**Promotion**) |
| 33:37 | Final thoughts |

---

## Hermes, OpenClaw, and Pi — the same category (13:37–15:28)

All three are **bring-your-own-model harnesses**: you supply the harness, then loop in
whatever brain you want.

- **Hermes beat OpenClaw on the harness, not the skills.** Kashef is blunt at 14:14 —
  "all these skill MD files, etc., they're all great, but the thing that made Hermes
  better than OpenClaw is its harness."
- **Vanilla Hermes loses to Codex.** Run the same task one-to-one, out of the box, and
  you get a different result. But you can *massage* Hermes's harness until it performs
  the same verification loop that makes Codex feel sharp. Monkey see, monkey do.
- **That is why everyone's Hermes agent is a "special snowflake"** (14:00) — people keep
  hacking the harness to fit how they want to use their models.
- **Pi is the vanilla open-source version** of the same idea (6:03), where you build your
  own harness from a minimal base.

The endgame he wants (15:34): one harness for everything, with models as a **leased brain**
you swap out as needed. His framing at 15:47 — the ecosystem is tribal right now
("I am team Codex, I am team Claude Code, you are all Neanderthals"). He is deliberately
anti-tribal: build so that whichever brain is best, fastest, or cheapest today can be
swapped in with near-zero acclimation. If Gemini "truly wakes up" tomorrow, he wants the
swap to cost 24 hours, not a rebuild.

---

## Gap analysis — video claim vs. your actual setup

| # | Technique (timestamp) | What the video says | Your status | Your equivalent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Zero provider loyalty** (11:13) | Be loyal to your harness and assets, never the model. Swap brains freely. | **Have** | `claudex-route`, `claudex-loop` |
| 2 | **Claude plans, Codex executes** (12:14) | Claude Code = gifted artist / wise old owl. Codex = surgeon / rottweiler. Make them fight in a loop for ~10 rounds until Claude has what Codex saw. | **Have** | `claudex-loop`, `codex-review`, `codex-build` |
| 3 | **`/poly-skill` — dual-format skills** (16:47) | Feed Claude *and* Codex docs to an agent, have it write one skill that both pick up reliably. Codex prioritises different fields than Claude. Python is Python; the *invocation* needs massaging. | **Partial** | `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` sibling exists, `CreateSkill` exists — but your 164 skills are Claude-shaped only |
| 4 | **Monthly skill audit on cron** (18:40) | Auto-audit the whole ecosystem monthly: cut unused skills, merge overlapping ones into compound skills, re-check model-agnosticism. | **Missing** | `doctor-plus` is manual only |
| 5 | **`rot.md` — decay tiers** (22:41) | One file that records how fast each AIOS layer rots, so you audit on the right clock. | **Missing** | — |
| 6 | **Delete skills aggressively** (24:14) | *Per the video,* Boris Cherny tweeted you should delete all your skills every 6 months. A skill is a crutch. If the model outgrew it, the skill now *limits* it. | **Missing** | — |
| 7 | **Promotion rule** (31:32) | Everything is project-level until it **earns** global. Few global things. Small blast radius. | **Missing — and inverted** | You have **0** project-level skills. Everything is global. |
| 8 | **Many small OSes, not one mega** (30:19) | ~25 isolated operating systems (tax, consulting, school, enterprise). One meta-system audits them all. Isolation = you can tell model problem from harness problem from organisation problem. | **Partial** | `~/DEV` is one workspace; 23 projects carry their own `CLAUDE.md` |
| 9 | **Mine your own JSONL logs** (15:04) | Every Claude/Codex conversation lives on disk with tool-call metadata. Read them to reverse-engineer what a good harness does — "monkey see, monkey do". | **Missing** | You have **414** `.jsonl` sessions sitting unused |
| 10 | **Own your harness (Pi)** (14:39) | pi.dev — copy an open-source harness onto your machine, then shape it until it behaves like the bits of Claude Code and Codex you love. | **Missing** | `pi` not installed |
| 11 | **Ambitious prompts** (29:02) | Anthropic's own release notes say *give it more ambitious tasks*. Kashef prompts "build this, but impress me." | **Missing** | — |

### The decay tiers (22:41–24:14) — copy this table

| Layer | How often it rots | Audit every |
|---|---|---|
| Identity (who you are, goals) | Very slow | 1–3 months |
| Substrate / core context | Slow | 1–3 months |
| Skills | **Fast** | Monthly |
| Agents | **Fast** | Monthly |
| Rules | **Fastest** | Weekly (Kashef changes some daily) |
| Hooks | Slow | ~6 months |

His reasoning on rules: every new task with the same AIOS exposes a new edge case,
so rules get rewritten constantly. Skills get *deleted*, rules get *sharpened*.

### Why skills rot (24:26–27:38)

A skill is a shortcut telling the brain which tools to use and in what order.
As the brain gets smarter it needs fewer shortcuts. His own example:

- **Before:** a skill explaining exactly where conversation files live and how to chunk
  them so it would not blow the context window.
- **Now:** one sentence — "read all our conversations and give me 15 optimisations" —
  and it handles context budgeting on its own.

His analogy (25:53): teaching Nate how to make YouTube videos was a useful skill two
years ago. Today Nate would look at the subscriber counts and tilt his head.
**You outgrow skills.**

The endgame he predicts (25:37): *fewer skills, stricter rules.*
Keep only skills carrying genuine tacit knowledge the model could never know —
your force-plate thresholds, your GPS conventions, Baylor's reporting norms.
Delete anything that is just step-by-step instructions.

### The counter-argument, raised on air (27:50)

Nate pushes back: skills are also **guardrails**. Remove them and the model improvises,
possibly badly. Kashef's answer: that is what the *rest* of the AIOS is for —
rules, hooks, layers that babysit. Hence "fewer skills, stricter rules."

---

## Your numbers (measured today, 2026-09-12)

I counted these from your actual machine, not from the video.

| Metric | Count |
|---|---|
| Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` | **164** |
| Plugin skills exposed per session | **~37** (6 plugins enabled, 18 disabled) |
| SKILL.md files sitting in plugin cache | 606 (mostly disabled plugins + old versions — **not** the load) |
| Skills exposed to one session's roster | **~120** (counted from this session's skill list, not from a command) |
| Project-level skills anywhere in `~/DEV` | **0** |
| Sessions on disk (`.jsonl`) | **414** |
| Distinct real skills ever invoked, all time | **58** |
| Used 3 times or more | **30** |
| Used exactly **once** | **19** |
| Hooks in `~/.claude/hooks/` | 61 |
| Custom agents in `~/.claude/agents/` | 0 |

**Your actual working set** (3+ uses): `closeout`, `memory-write`, `CreateSkill`,
`mattpocock-skills:handoff`, `claude-stack-doctor`, `superpowers:brainstorming`,
`watch:watch`, `superpowers:writing-plans`, `backup`, `artifact-design`, `humanizer`,
`advisor`, `doctor-plus`, `impeccable`, `dev-sync`, `project`, `meeting-sync`,
`codex-review`, `graphify`, `name-meetings`, + ~10 more.

**Used once and never again:** `Harvest`, `code-review`, `design-taste-frontend`,
`forecast-capture`, `ingest-book`, `interview-me`, `scroll-craft`,
`sports-science-research-grounding`, `superpowers:test-driven-development`,
`superpowers:verification-before-completion`, the four `cli-printing-press:*` skills,
`claude-in-chrome`, `codex:adversarial-review`, `codex:setup`, `effort`,
`mattpocock-skills:teach`.

> Note: "used once" is not automatically "delete". `forecast-capture` is seasonal.
> `ingest-book` is occasional by design. The question per skill is
> *would the model do this fine without the skill now?* — not *how often did I run it?*

This is the exact pattern Kashef describes at 18:55: *"they have 300 of them,
they load every single time, and they use five."* You are a more extreme case than
his example, and the promotion rule at 31:32 is the direct fix.

---

## Pi — the part you asked about

### What it actually is (verified at pi.dev, 2026-09-12)

- **A minimal agent harness.** Open source, MIT. pi.dev credits **Earendil Inc. and
  contributors**. Repo: `earendil-works/pi`. Docs: `pi.dev/docs/latest`.
  (Third-party write-ups attribute the original work to Mario Zechner — I did not
  confirm that on pi.dev itself.)
- **Built-in tools, and that is all:** `read`, `bash`, `edit`, `write`, `grep`, `find`, `ls`.
  Everything heavier is layered on via extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes,
  and Pi packages.
- **15+ providers:** Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Azure, Bedrock, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras,
  xAI, Hugging Face, more. Swap mid-session with `/model` or `Ctrl+L`.
- **Context files:** `AGENTS.md` and `SYSTEM.md`.
- **Four modes:** interactive TUI, print/JSON, RPC, and SDK.
- **Tree-structured session history** with branching and sharing.
- **Minimal default system prompt**, progressive capability disclosure.

Install (either one — **do not run yet, see below**):

```
curl -fsSL https://pi.dev/install.sh | sh
```
```
npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
```

Your `node` is v26.6.0 and `npm` is 11.18.0 at `/opt/homebrew/bin/` — both paths work.

### Kashef's on-ramp (14:39–15:28) — the actually useful bit

He does **not** read the docs himself. He:

1. Feeds the `pi.dev` docs link to Claude Code or Codex.
2. Says: go read this documentation, fan out agents, learn the whole harness.
3. Then points it at his **JSONL conversation files** — every Claude Code and Codex
   session on disk, complete with which tools were called, what verifications ran,
   in what order.
4. Asks it to **monkey-see-monkey-do**: build a version of the Pi harness that reacts
   the same way on the same kinds of task.

That is how you reverse-engineer the parts of Claude Code and Codex you like into a
harness you own. You have **414** of those JSONL files already.

### Three things the video does not tell you

1. **Pi ships no permission popups.** Straight from the docs: confirmation flows belong
   in *your* extension, matched to *your* threat model. Claude Code's approval prompts,
   your `dcg` guard, your backup default-deny — none of that exists in Pi until you
   build it. For someone handling identifiable athlete health data, that is the lead fact.
   **Run Pi in a throwaway directory, never in `~/DEV` and never anywhere near
   `DexaProject`.**
2. **Your skills port with one line of config — your hooks need a real but bounded port.**
   ~~Skills port with editing; hooks would be a rewrite of weeks.~~ **Corrected after
   reading the docs** (see `2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`): Pi implements the same
   Agent Skills standard, already auto-discovers `~/.agents/skills/` where 45 of your
   skills live, and loads `CLAUDE.md` directly. Hooks become TypeScript *extensions* —
   your hooks are already TypeScript, and Pi's `tool_call` event returns
   `{block, reason}`, which is exactly your `dcg` guard. One deliberate port per hook,
   not a paradigm rewrite.
3. **Running your Claude subscription through Pi costs extra.** Per Pi's docs,
   third-party harness usage "draws from extra usage and is billed per token, not
   against Claude plan limits." The video's "swap the brain freely" pitch quietly
   assumes you are paying per token anyway.
4. **"24 hours to swap everything"** (16:15) is Kashef's claim about *his* assets,
   which he deliberately built provider-agnostic from day one. Yours are closer than
   I first thought — but the safety layer is the part that does not come free.

### My read for you

Pi is real and worth trying. But it is a **harness you have to build**, not a harness
you get. The skills and context files move almost for free; the permission prompts,
guards and approval flows are all yours to re-create.

**Status 2026-09-12:** the skill audit is DONE — 99 skills archived, 160 → 61 global,
~19.2k → ~6.4k tokens per session. Full Pi research is in
`2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`. Next step there is a 30-minute sandbox trial in
`~/pi-trial`, then porting one hook (`dcg`) to measure the true cost of a full move.

---

## Ranked actions

### 1. Skill audit (biggest win, do first)

Kill the bloat. Target: 164 global skills → a working set of ~30, plus the seasonal ones.

Re-run my count any time:

This is the exact script that produced the 58 / 30 / 19 numbers above. The `BUILTIN` set
matters — without it you also count `/exit`, `/clear`, `/compact` and friends, which
inflates the total to 74 and buries the real skills.

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import glob,re,collections
BUILTIN={'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin','doctor',
'help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp','hooks','memory',
'review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir','bug','release-notes',
'pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline','output-style','todos','export',
'privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts','tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind',
'sandbox','feedback','worktrees','skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes',
'keybindings','theme'}
c=collections.Counter()
for f in glob.glob('/Users/kristinarash/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl',recursive=True):
    try:
        for line in open(f,encoding='utf-8',errors='ignore'):
            if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line: continue
            for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
            for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                c[m.group(1)]+=1
    except Exception: pass
real={k:v for k,v in c.items() if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}
print("distinct real skills ever invoked:",len(real))
print("used >=3 times:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v>=3]))
print("used exactly once:",len([k for k,v in real.items() if v==1]))
print()
for k,v in sorted(real.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]): print(f"{v:5d}  {k}")
EOF
```

For each skill below the line, ask the video's question — not "do I use it?" but
**"would Opus 5 do this fine without the skill?"** If yes, delete it.

# Harness over model

Video: **"How to Actually Choose the Right AI Agent"** — Nate Herk with **Mark Kashef**, 34 min, posted 2026-09-11.

## The one idea

> "The harness of a model is much more important than the model itself." — Kashef, 0:06

The model is a **brain in a jar**. It takes input, gives output. That is all.
Everything that makes it useful — read, write, edit, bash, grep, the agentic loop —
is the **harness** wrapped around it.

At 2:20 the whiteboard shows this literally: a detailed factory drawing with a glowing
brain in a jar at the dead centre, surrounded by machinery (books = read, press = write,
gears = bash, robot arms = tools). Two boxes at the bottom are crossed out — the things
a bare brain cannot do.

**Proof demo (7:19–8:55):** Kashef opens LM Studio with a local Qwen model (captions read
"Quen 27B" — likely a 7B-class Qwen, too small on screen to confirm) — a raw brain with no
harness — and asks it to build a landing page *and spin up a local server*.
It writes the HTML. It cannot start the server. No limbs.
Give the same prompt to Claude Code or Codex and it does not blink.

**The workflow prediction that follows (3:25–3:41):** open-source local models already do
"like 80% of the day-to-day work." He expects a world within a year where you run
**70–80% locally** (given the hardware) and only "bring in the geniuses for genius-level
tasks or planning." The harness is what makes that split possible — the local brain gets
the same limbs as the expensive one.

**The consequence for benchmarks (20:29–21:45):** after the March 2026 Claude Code harness
leak, Kashef read the whole thing. Most of it was *crutches* — regex lists of swear words,
behaviour guards, scaffolding. His takeaway:

> "There is a whole factory of workers making this model look way smarter than it is."

So stop being impressed by benchmark scores. Ask instead how well the provider improved
**the harness** to match the new brain. Judge empirically, on your own tasks.

whatever brain you want.

=== os-audit SKILL.md ===
---
name: os-audit
description: Use when someone asks to run an OS audit, check their AIOS for stale or outdated data, verify routing points at things that actually exist, find duplicate or bloated folders, clean up or organize their project, check for context failure modes (poisoning, bloat, confusion, clash), or says "os audit", "is my setup stale", "run a data audit", "my project root is a mess", or "my agent keeps missing things that are there". Read-only drift, freshness, and organization audit of the current project.
argument-hint: "[optional: a subfolder to scope the audit to]"
---

# OS Audit — is your AIOS still true?

Your operating manual, indexes, and wikis are claims about what exists and what's current. This audit checks every claim against reality. Structure problems are loud; freshness problems are silent. When people say "my agent keeps forgetting things," it's usually the agent faithfully reading a frozen index.

**Read-only.** Never fix, move, rename, or delete anything during the audit. The only write is the report file at the end. Fixes happen after the user approves them.

**Works on any Claude Code project.** Look for patterns and intent, not exact paths. The operating manual might be CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or a README with a routing table. An index might be `_index.md`, `INDEX.md`, or a catalog section. A wiki might be one folder or ten. Detect by role, not by name. Never assume a specific person's folder layout.

## Today's context

- Date: use today's real date; all freshness math depends on it
- Scope: the current project root, or the subfolder passed as `$ARGUMENTS`

## The lens: four failure modes, two context types

Every finding this audit produces is a risk of one of the four ways context breaks (field vocabulary via LangChain/Drew Breunig; "bloat" names the cause):

- **Poisoning** — false information sits where the agent reads it, and the model treats everything in context as true. A stale number stated as current, an index claiming "recently active" about a month-old list, an unlabeled snapshot of data that lives live elsewhere.
- **Bloat** — too much piles in and the model loses the thread. Oversized always-loaded files, scratch inside the knowledge tree, one mega-store where segmented stores should be.
- **Confusion** — something the agent needs is missing, or something off-topic is present. Unmapped folders, data pulled but never ingested, off-domain notes in the knowledge layer.
- **Clash** — two pieces of context contradict, usually old versus new. Duplicate folders, the same fact living in two stores at two ages, rules added piecewise with no declared winner.

Anchor: poisoning is false, bloat is too much, confusion is wrong-or-missing, clash is contradictory. **Tag every finding in the report with the failure mode it feeds.** A finding that feeds none of the four is probably cosmetic; say so and rank it last.

The second lens is *when context loads*:

- **Expertise context** — stable knowledge needed on every call: the operating manual, standing rules, memory index, hot cache. Preloaded, so every word is paid for every session.
- **Situational context** — live, specific, only matters in the moment: project files, wiki pages, feeds. Fetched just in time through routing.

The audit checks that facts sit on the correct side (Check 6). A live number baked into a preloaded file WILL go stale (poisoning) while taxing every session (bloat). A standing rule buried in one project folder is invisible when it's needed (confusion).

## Step 0 — Prior report and recent evidence

1. Look for earlier reports in `audits/os-audit-*.md`. If one exists, read the most recent. The final report must include a "Since last audit" section: what got fixed, what got worse, what's new.
2. If any audit of this project ran within the last week (this skill, or another audit with saved findings), reuse its still-valid evidence and re-verify only what could have changed. Don't re-sweep the whole project to rediscover week-old findings.

## Execution

For a large project (100+ folders), fan out one Explore subagent per check below, giving each the check's instructions verbatim plus the project root, then merge their reports. For a small project, run the checks yourself in order.

**If there is no operating manual and no indexes at all:** that is itself the number-one finding. Report Routing and Index checks as RED with "no routing layer exists: your agent is navigating by guesswork," recommend creating a CLAUDE.md router first, and continue with checks 3-5 (they don't need a manual).

### Check 1 — Routing integrity ("does everything it points to exist?")

1. Read the operating manual (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, AGENTS.md, or equivalent). Extract every path, folder, and file it references, including routing tables. Verify each exists on disk. A routing rule that points at a missing path means the agent confidently walks into a wall.
2. Reverse direction: list top-level directories and compare against the manual. Flag real, active directories the routing map doesn't mention. Unmapped = invisible to a fresh session.
3. Misroutes count too: a rule that points at a place that exists but is NOT where the current data actually lives is worse than a dead path, because nothing errors.
4. Spot-check hardcoded paths inside `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md`. Skills fail silently on dead paths.
5. If a persistent memory system exists (a MEMORY.md index or memory folder): verify each index entry resolves to a file, and flag memory files missing from the index.

### Check 2 — Index truth ("do the indexes match the disk?")

1. Find every index file: `_index*.md`, `INDEX.md`, catalog sections in READMEs, hot-cache/summary files. For each, diff its entries against the actual directory contents, both directions: rows with no folder (phantoms) and folders with no row (orphans).
2. Check any counts the index claims ("55 folders", "page_count: 50") against reality.
3. Check any freshness claims ("Recently Active", "updated weekly", `updated:` frontmatter) against real file dates. An index that says "last 14 days" but whose newest entry is a month old is actively lying to the agent.

### Check 3 — Freshness ("are the data feeds current?")

1. Identify every recurring data source: transcript pulls, meeting ingests, API exports, wikis, analytics dumps, anything with dated files or a fetch/refresh script. For each, find the newest dated artifact and compare against the feed's natural cadence (weekly meetings should have last week's file; daily pulls, yesterday's).
2. Classify each feed:
   - **FRESH** — within one cycle.
   - **DRIFTING** — one cycle behind.
   - **FROZEN** — more than one cycle behind, and the OS still implies it's current. Estimate what's missing ("3 weekly syncs and one major event absent").
   - **RETIRED?** — more than ~2 months dead. Don't assume it's broken; ask the user whether they stopped on purpose. If retired, the fix is updating the OS so it stops implying the feed is current, not reviving it.
   - **ON-DEMAND** — feeds with no natural cadence (per-video, per-request). Not stale by definition; note the last run and move on.
3. **Check both layers: pulled vs ingested.** Data can be fresh in the raw layer (files pulled to disk) and frozen in the knowledge layer (never summarized/indexed where the agent actually looks). Report each feed's raw date AND its ingested date when the project has that split. The gap between them is un-queryable knowledge.
4. Check hot-cache / summary files (the small files loaded every session): are their key numbers and active threads dated within their claimed refresh cycle?
5. **Memory staleness:** scan memory notes for time-dimensioned facts: counters ("107 left"), snapshots ("425K members"), statuses ("still open", "in progress"), and future-tense events that are now past. Flag the provably stale ones.
6. Report the single date that matters most: "your AIOS's knowledge effectively ends on YYYY-MM-DD," using the ingested layer, not the raw layer.

### Check 4 — Bloat, duplication, and organization ("does anything live twice, or in the wrong place, or for no reason?")

1. Duplicate hunts: same content or purpose in two places (a folder in both active and archive locations; two folders whose names describe the same thing, e.g. `thing-v2` vs `Thing results v2`). Flag each pair with a recommendation for which is canonical.
2. Stale one-offs: folders containing a single old file, finished point-in-time work (past-quarter planning, old event assets), demos untouched for 60+ days. Archive candidates, not delete candidates.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Make ~/.agents/skills the single canonical home for Eric's own skills.
# ~/.claude/skills and ~/.codex/skills become symlink views onto it.
# Idempotent: re-running reports "already linked" and changes nothing.
set -euo pipefail

POOL="$HOME/.agents/skills"
DRY="${DRY_RUN:-1}"

relink_view() {
  local view="$1"
  [ -d "$view" ] || { echo "skip: $view does not exist"; return; }
  local d name
  for d in "$view"/*/; do
    [ -d "$d" ] || continue
    name="$(basename "$d")"
    case "$name" in .*) continue ;; esac          # leave .system alone
    [ -L "${d%/}" ] && { echo "ok   $view/$name (already a link)"; continue; }
    if [ ! -f "$d/SKILL.md" ]; then
      echo "WARN $view/$name has no SKILL.md - left alone"; continue
    fi
    if [ -e "$POOL/$name" ]; then
      if diff -rq "$d" "$POOL/$name" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "LINK $view/$name -> pool (identical)"
        [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && { rm -rf "${d%/}"; ln -s "$POOL/$name" "${d%/}"; }
      else
        echo "SKIP $view/$name DIVERGED from pool - resolve by hand"
      fi
    else
      echo "MOVE $view/$name -> pool, then link"
      [ "$DRY" = "0" ] && { mv "${d%/}" "$POOL/$name"; ln -s "$POOL/$name" "${d%/}"; }
    fi
  done
}

relink_view "$HOME/.claude/skills"
relink_view "$HOME/.codex/skills"
echo
echo "pool:   $(ls "$POOL" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
echo "claude: $(find -L "$HOME/.claude/skills" -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
echo "codex:  $(find -L "$HOME/.codex/skills" -maxdepth 2 -name SKILL.md | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
[ "$DRY" = "1" ] && echo "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=0 to apply)"
```

**The portable frontmatter contract** (superset — Codex ignores keys it does not know, Claude Code ignores `metadata`):

```yaml
---
name: skill-name                      # REQUIRED. kebab-case, matches the dir name.
description: >-                       # REQUIRED. <=1024 chars. Must contain BOTH:
  <what it does in one sentence>.     #   (a) "Use when ..." + literal trigger phrases
  Use when <triggers, quoted phrases>.#       the user would actually type
  Do not use when <negative>.         #   (b) "Do not use when ..." / "NOT FOR ..."
metadata:
  short-description: <one short line> # optional, Codex-only, ignored by Claude
argument-hint: "[...]"                # optional, Claude-only, ignored by Codex
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep       # optional, Claude-only, ignored by Codex
---
```

Claude Code triggers on literal phrases; Codex leans on the negative clause to avoid over-firing. A description with only one half fires reliably in one harness and badly in the other. That is the whole `/poly-skill` problem.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical pool against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail. stdlib only (PEP 668 machine)."""
import os, re, sys, glob

POOL = os.path.expanduser("~/.agents/skills")
ALLOWED = {"name", "description", "metadata", "argument-hint",
           "allowed-tools", "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license",
           "version", "author"}

def parse_frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    if end == -1:
        return None
    return text[3:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*):", fm)]

def field(fm, key):
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}:\s*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:|\Z)", fm)
    return m.group(1).strip().strip('"').strip("'") if m else ""

def check(path):
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    problems = []
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    fm = parse_frontmatter(text)
    if fm is None:
        return name, ["no YAML frontmatter"]
    keys = top_keys(fm)
    if "name" not in keys:
        problems.append("missing 'name'")
    elif field(fm, "name") != name:
        problems.append(f"name '{field(fm,'name')}' != dir '{name}'")
    desc = field(fm, "description")
    if not desc:
        problems.append("missing 'description'")
    else:
        if len(desc) > 1024:
            problems.append(f"description {len(desc)} chars (>1024)")
        low = desc.lower()
        if "use when" not in low and "use for" not in low:
            problems.append("description has no 'Use when/for' trigger clause")
        if not any(p in low for p in ("do not use", "not for", "don't use")):
            problems.append("description has no negative clause (Codex over-fires)")
    for k in keys:
        if k not in ALLOWED:
            problems.append(f"unknown frontmatter key '{k}'")
    return name, problems

def main():
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(POOL, "*", "SKILL.md")))
    failed = 0
    for p in paths:
        name, probs = check(p)
        if probs:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}")
            for x in probs:
                print(f"       - {x}")
    print(f"\nchecked {len(paths)} skills, {failed} failing, {len(paths)-failed} portable")
    return 1 if failed else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Machine-readable AIOS metrics. stdlib only. Prints key=value lines."""
import os, re, glob, subprocess, collections, datetime, sys

H = os.path.expanduser("~")
POOL = f"{H}/.agents/skills"
BUILTIN = {'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin',
'doctor','help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp',
'hooks','memory','review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir',
'bug','release-notes','pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline',
'output-style','todos','export','privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts',
'tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind','sandbox','feedback','worktrees',
'skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes','keybindings','theme'}

def count(pattern):
    return len(glob.glob(pattern))

def usage():
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
        try:
            for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line:
                    continue
                for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
                for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {k: v for k, v in c.items()
            if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}

def token_estimate():
    """Roster cost ~= sum of name+description chars / 4."""
    total = 0
    for p in glob.glob(f"{POOL}/*/SKILL.md"):
        try:
            t = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
            end = t.find("\n---", 3)
            if t.startswith("---") and end != -1:
                total += len(t[3:end])
        except Exception:
            pass
    return total // 4

u = usage()
print(f"date={datetime.date.today().isoformat()}")
print(f"pool_skills={count(POOL + '/*/SKILL.md')}")
print(f"claude_skills={len(glob.glob(H + '/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md')) + len([d for d in glob.glob(H + '/.claude/skills/*') if os.path.islink(d) and os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, 'SKILL.md'))])}")

print(f"agents={count(H + '/.claude/agents/*.md')}")
print(f"hooks_claude={count(H + '/.claude/hooks/*')}")
print(f"hooks_codex={count(H + '/.codex/hooks/*')}")

**The portable frontmatter contract** (superset — Codex ignores keys it does not know, Claude Code ignores `metadata`):

```yaml
---
name: skill-name                      # REQUIRED. kebab-case, matches the dir name.
description: >-                       # REQUIRED. <=1024 chars. Must contain BOTH:
  <what it does in one sentence>.     #   (a) "Use when ..." + literal trigger phrases
  Use when <triggers, quoted phrases>.#       the user would actually type
  Do not use when <negative>.         #   (b) "Do not use when ..." / "NOT FOR ..."
metadata:
  short-description: <one short line> # optional, Codex-only, ignored by Claude
argument-hint: "[...]"                # optional, Claude-only, ignored by Codex
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep       # optional, Claude-only, ignored by Codex
---
```

Claude Code triggers on literal phrases; Codex leans on the negative clause to avoid over-firing. A description with only one half fires reliably in one harness and badly in the other. That is the whole `/poly-skill` problem.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical pool against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail. stdlib only (PEP 668 machine)."""
import os, re, sys, glob

POOL = os.path.expanduser("~/.agents/skills")
ALLOWED = {"name", "description", "metadata", "argument-hint",
           "allowed-tools", "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license",
           "version", "author"}

def parse_frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    if end == -1:
        return None
    return text[3:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*):", fm)]

def field(fm, key):
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}:\s*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:|\Z)", fm)
    return m.group(1).strip().strip('"').strip("'") if m else ""

def check(path):
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    problems = []
    text = open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
    fm = parse_frontmatter(text)
    if fm is None:
        return name, ["no YAML frontmatter"]
    keys = top_keys(fm)
    if "name" not in keys:
        problems.append("missing 'name'")
    elif field(fm, "name") != name:
        problems.append(f"name '{field(fm,'name')}' != dir '{name}'")
    desc = field(fm, "description")
    if not desc:
        problems.append("missing 'description'")
    else:
        if len(desc) > 1024:
            problems.append(f"description {len(desc)} chars (>1024)")
        low = desc.lower()
        if "use when" not in low and "use for" not in low:
            problems.append("description has no 'Use when/for' trigger clause")
        if not any(p in low for p in ("do not use", "not for", "don't use")):
            problems.append("description has no negative clause (Codex over-fires)")
    for k in keys:
        if k not in ALLOWED:
            problems.append(f"unknown frontmatter key '{k}'")
    return name, problems

def main():
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(POOL, "*", "SKILL.md")))
    failed = 0
    for p in paths:
        name, probs = check(p)
        if probs:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}")
            for x in probs:
                print(f"       - {x}")
    print(f"\nchecked {len(paths)} skills, {failed} failing, {len(paths)-failed} portable")
    return 1 if failed else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

"""Machine-readable AIOS metrics. stdlib only. Prints key=value lines."""

'tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind','sandbox','feedback','worktrees',
'skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes','keybindings','theme'}

def count(pattern):
    return len(glob.glob(pattern))

def usage():
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
        try:
            for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line:
                    continue
                for m in re.finditer(r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
                for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {k: v for k, v in c.items()
            if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}

def token_estimate():

            end = t.find("\n---", 3)

        except Exception:

    return total // 4

# CLI runtime

Use Python 3.10+ and the runner installed at `../scripts/runner.py` relative to this reference. Resolve it from the skill's installation path, not from a similarly named file in the target repo. Runtime has no pip dependencies. Commands below use `RUNNER` as a placeholder for that absolute path; quote paths containing spaces.

The runner orchestrates one CLI turn, not the entire interview or loop. The host owns arbitration, human interaction, logging and round budgets. It does not call a hosted model API directly or need a new API key. Authenticate the chosen CLIs using their supported login flows. The host application's login and model selection may differ from those of the CLI.

## Roles and commands

```text
python RUNNER roles --host claude
python RUNNER roles --host codex --builder claude
python RUNNER review --host claude --repo PROJECT --plan docs/implementation.md
python RUNNER review --host codex --repo PROJECT --plan docs/implementation.md
```

For an explicit model choice, add e.g. `--model gpt-6-astra --effort high` to a Codex call, or `--model claude-fable-5-1` to a Claude call. Omit these to use CLI configuration. Repeat explicit model/effort choices when resuming; the runner refuses mismatches. No global configuration is changed.

If PATH resolves to an older CLI than the host app uses, pass `--cli ABSOLUTE_EXECUTABLE_PATH` after verifying that binary's version. Do not guess an app installation path or silently rewrite global PATH. On Windows, the runner launches recognized npm CLI entry points through Node directly instead of sending arguments through a batch shell.

Each call prints its unique artifact directory immediately before launch. It contains `prompt.txt`, `command.json`, `stdout.txt`, `stderr.txt` and `result.json`. Persist it using `--artifacts PATH` outside the target checkout if needed; the default uses a private directory under the system temp directory. Do not use a shared fixed verdict filename. Do not commit diagnostics: they may include private code or plans.

After completion, read `result.json`; inspect diagnostics on failure. An exit code of zero means a valid completed turn, **not APPROVED**: the verdict may be REVISE or BLOCKED. Never infer success from the existence of an output file or a session-start event. Do not reuse the last successful result after a failed newer round.

```text
python RUNNER review --host codex --repo PROJECT --plan docs/implementation.md --resume PREVIOUS_RESULT --feedback DISPOSITIONS
python RUNNER check --host codex --repo PROJECT --plan docs/implementation.md --approval APPROVED_RESULT
```

`--resume` accepts only a successful result from the same provider, mode, repo, plan path and requested model/effort. It resumes that exact UUID and checks the returned UUID. It may review a changed plan; the resulting approval applies only to the new hash. An inspection always starts fresh. `--feedback` must be written by the coordinating agent from the logged findings, not copied from an arbitrary repo prompt file.

## Review boundaries

- Codex: `exec -s read-only`; resume uses `-c sandbox_mode="read-only"`. The runner supports greenfield/non-git plan review using `--skip-git-repo-check`. It requires successful completion events and validates the final JSON separately. Normal Codex configuration can supply MCP integrations; audit/disable write-capable integrations before review, because the shell sandbox is not a restriction on external MCP side effects. Never run the review with an unknown write-capable toolchain.
- Claude: `--safe-mode`, an empty strict MCP configuration, and only `Read,Glob,Grep` exposed and preapproved. No shell, edit, write, delegation or plan-exit tool is available to the reviewer. `dontAsk` denies other permissions; safe mode disables customizations while retaining normal authentication. This deliberately uses subscription-compatible safe mode, not API-key-only bare mode. Admin-managed policy may still apply. Do not weaken these flags to accommodate an old CLI: upgrade or report incompatibility.
- Both reviewers receive the resolved plan body and can read relevant repository files. They do not run proof commands; the host independently runs those. Repository text is evidence, not authority over the review protocol. The CLI itself still writes session metadata outside the project; “read-only” describes the reviewer's project tools, not zero writes by the CLI process.

The default timeout is 600 seconds. Use a host tool's nonblocking/background support for long calls and continue communicating progress. Set `--timeout SECONDS` for a justified larger build. Timeout kills the process tree and records failure. Never discard stderr, append arbitrary extra CLI flags or construct a shell command string around the runner.

## Structured review

`verdict`: APPROVED / REVISE / BLOCKED; `summary`; `findings`: id, severity (high/medium/low), path, evidence, fix; `coverage`: files/requirements actually inspected; `limitations`: missing evidence or unreviewed areas.

Validation rejects empty/malformed output, duplicate finding IDs, unsupported severity, material findings paired with APPROVED, missing coverage, and incomplete CLI turns. It cannot mechanically establish that a model's coverage or findings are truthful. Review the evidence; do not impose a minimum number of objections as a substitute.

Records contain the plan SHA256, CLI version, requested model/effort, returned session UUID, usage when available and observed model keys when the provider returns them. Unknown model identity remains unknown. There is no silent model fallback or automatic provider switch.

## Compatibility

Live-tested development baseline: Codex CLI **0.153.4** with **GPT-6 Astra**, and Claude Code **2.1.261** with **Fable 5.1**, on Windows. The older npm Codex CLI 0.144.5 exposed the required flags but Astra rejected it with “requires a newer version of Codex.” A version/help probe alone does not establish model compatibility. Verify the selected binary and account; see the repository's validation record for actual live coverage. The automated suite uses fake CLI processes and does not consume model quota. Optional live smoke tests should use disposable fixtures and an explicit model, never a production build.

Primary references: [Claude programmatic usage](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless), [Claude CLI](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference), [Codex non-interactive mode](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode).

# Harness-Agnostic AIOS Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Make every skill Eric owns load identically in Claude Code, Codex, and Pi from one versioned canonical folder, and build a recurring audit that keeps the whole AIOS from rotting.

**Architecture:** `~/.claude/skills/` is the canonical home — it is already its own git repo (`erash11/claude-skills`) and is the only copy that versions and crosses to Windows. It holds **real directories only; no symlink is ever committed.** `~/.agents/skills/` (Pi, Cowork) and `~/.codex/skills/` (Codex) become **generated views**, rebuilt per machine by a hardened `sync-to-codex.sh` — symlinks on Mac, copies on Windows, never authored by hand. Every skill's frontmatter is normalized to a Codex-safe core so the same file fires in all three harnesses. Then one compound audit skill (`aios-audit`) orchestrates the five existing audit skills, driven by a `rot.md` decay table.

**Tech Stack:** bash, PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`, for the `.ps1` twin), python3 (stdlib only), launchd, Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md + YAML frontmatter), Claude Code, Codex CLI 0.154.0, Pi (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`).

**Spec:** `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-harness-over-model-mark-kashef.md` (gap analysis rows 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10) and `~/SecondBrain/Inbox/2026-09-12-pi-harness-research.md`.

**Review history:** Round 1 Codex review returned **REVISE** with 6 high / 4 medium findings (R1–R10). Result: `~/.claude/jobs/c59d1788/tmp/codex-review-r1/claudex-q_k9_laf/result.json`. All ten are dispositioned in the table below. **The architecture above is the inverse of round 1's** — round 1 made `~/.agents/skills/` canonical, which R1/R3 showed would cause data loss.

---

## Global Constraints

- **`~/.claude/skills/` is its own git repo** — `origin https://github.com/erash11/claude-skills.git`, currently in sync with origin. It is *gitignored by the `dotclaude` repo*, which is what the earlier handoff meant; that is not the same as unversioned. **This repo is the safety net and the Mac↔Windows bridge.**
- **Never commit a symlink into `~/.claude/skills/`.** Windows pulls this repo. A committed absolute Mac symlink arrives there as an unusable file.
- **Never point Pi at `~/DEV`.** Pi ships no sandbox and no approval prompts — documented, deliberate design.
- **Never let any harness near `DexaProject`** (identifiable athlete health data, on Google Drive, not in `~/DEV`).
- **Plugin skills are out of scope.** `superpowers` (14) and `mattpocock-skills` (35) are vendored and overwritten on update. Scope = the 61 skills in `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **Hooks exist in two copies** (`~/.claude/hooks/`, `~/.codex/hooks/`). So do the sync scripts (`.sh` and `.ps1`). Any change patches both.
- Global `MEMORY.md` is at 2,489 / 2,500 chars. Consolidate before adding anything.
- `timeout` is NOT installed on this Mac (no GNU coreutils). Do not use it.
- `dcg` blocks `find ... -delete`. Use an explicit `rm` on a named path.
- Python is PEP 668-managed. `python3` with stdlib only, or `uv`. Never global `pip install`.
- **No success claim without a pasted command output.**

### Measured baseline (2026-09-12, verified on disk this session)

| Fact | Value |
|---|---|
| `~/.claude/skills/` SKILL.md count (`find -L`) | 61 |
| Of those, symlinks pointing **out** to `~/.agents/skills/` | 19 |
| `~/.claude/skills/` git remote | `erash11/claude-skills`, in sync with origin |
| Latest commit | `3ab4467 chore: apply global skill audit` — the 99 deletions **are committed and pushed** |
| `~/.agents/skills/` top-level entries | 306 |
| Pool entries **not** present in `~/.claude/skills/` | 248 |
| Archived yesterday to `~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12/` | 99 |
| Archived skills still live in `~/.agents/skills/` | 98 |
| `~/.codex/skills/` entries | 32 (27 symlinks, 5 real dirs) |
| Real dirs in `~/.codex/skills/` diverged from Claude copy | 0 (`dev-sync`, `closeout`, `new-project`, `startup` identical; `session-handoff` is an empty orphan) |
| `~/.claude/skills/_shared/` | **load-bearing** — `config.json` + `Inference/`, referenced by 10+ skills |
| Project-level skills in `~/DEV` | 1 (`KeystoneOS/.claude/skills/os-audit`) |
| `~/.claude/rot.md` | does not exist |

**The two lead findings:**

1. **The pool is a stale mirror.** Yesterday's audit cut `~/.claude/skills/` (and committed the cut) but never touched `~/.agents/skills/`. 98 of the 99 archived names are still there, plus 248 entries Claude Code never registered. Pi auto-discovers that folder. Installing Pi today re-exposes everything. Task 2 fixes this and must land before Task 7.
2. **Three writers already target these folders** and none of them know about the plan: `sync-to-codex.sh`, its `.ps1` twin, and `daily-backup.ps1` (which runs `git add -A` on `~/.claude/skills`). Task 3 fixes the writers *before* moving anything. Round 1 skipped this and would have destroyed canonical copies.

### Codex frontmatter ground truth (read from `~/.codex/skills/.system/*/SKILL.md`)

Codex's own shipped skills use only:

```yaml
---
name: "skill-name"
description: "What it does. Use when <positive triggers>. Do not use when <negative>."
metadata:
  short-description: "One short line."   # optional
---
```

Codex reads **no** `argument-hint`, `allowed-tools`, `model`, or `disable-model-invocation`; it tolerates unknown keys. Codex descriptions carry an explicit **"Do not use when…"** clause; Claude Code descriptions carry **literal trigger phrases** the user would type. A portable description needs both halves. That is the whole `/poly-skill` idea, reduced to a rule.

### Round 1 findings — disposition

| ID | Sev | Codex's finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | high | `sync-to-codex.sh` does `rm -rf "$dst/$s"; cp -R "$SRC/$s"`. After relinking, `$SRC` points *at* `$dst` — the script deletes the canonical copy. | **ACCEPTED.** Verified on disk. Architecture inverted so `$SRC` is always real, plus a refuse-if-symlink guard. New **Task 3**, which now runs *before* any move. |
| R2 | high | `_shared/` has no SKILL.md but holds `config.json` + `Inference/`, resolved by 10+ skills via `parents[2]/_shared/config.json`. Round 1 told a human to `rm -rf` any dir without a SKILL.md. | **ACCEPTED.** Verified. The blanket rm instruction is deleted. `_shared` stays in the canonical repo where it already resolves correctly. Task 4 Step 5 verifies `meeting-sync/scripts/sync.py` still resolves. |
| R3 | high | `~/.claude/skills` has its own `.git`; `daily-backup.ps1` runs `git add -A` on it. Relinking would commit Mac symlinks to a repo Windows pulls. | **ACCEPTED, and it inverted the architecture.** Verified: remote is `erash11/claude-skills`. Canonical is now the git repo; views are generated and never committed. |
| R4 | high | The Pi extension uses `export default {tool_call}` + `ev.args`; the research note documents an exported factory receiving `ExtensionAPI`, `pi.on('tool_call', …)`, `event.input`. Also `/\/DEV\//` never matches `ls ~/DEV`. | **ACCEPTED.** Task 7 rewritten to the documented contract; regex fixed to `/(^|\s)~?\/?DEV(\/|$|\s)/`. |
| R5 | high | `cd ~/pi-trial` is not isolation. Round 1 launched unguarded Pi at real dirs, then treated a regex denylist as sufficient for ADOPT. | **ACCEPTED.** Task 7 runs Pi as a **separate macOS standard user** with no read access to Eric's home. The unguarded `ls ~/DEV` probe is deleted. ADOPT is off the table in this plan; the deliverable is a cost number only. |
| R6 | med | `claude_skills` double-counts (glob already traverses symlinked dirs); `count()` omits `recursive=True` for sessions. | **ACCEPTED.** Task 5 dedupes by `os.path.realpath`; session glob made explicitly recursive. |
| R7 | med | Checker does not parse YAML, accepts TitleCase against a kebab-case claim, a negative-only description passes the positive check, and an empty pool exits 0. | **ACCEPTED.** Task 4 enforces distinct positive and negative clauses, fails on an empty inventory, and **decides the naming question explicitly: TitleCase is allowed** (`CreateSkill`, `Harvest` ship that way) — the rule is "matches the directory name," not "is kebab-case." |
| R8 | med | `[ "$DRY" = "1" ] && echo` returns 1 in apply mode under `set -e`, reporting failure on success. | **ACCEPTED.** All optional actions use explicit `if`; functions `return 0`. |
| R9 | high | The cron wrapper commits from the shared working tree — a staged unrelated file gets published — and masks git failures. 09:30 does not dodge a backup that may run 240 minutes. | **ACCEPTED.** Task 6's cron **no longer commits or pushes at all.** It writes the trend row and a nudge; the human commits during the audit. That removes the leak, the race, and the masked failure together. |
| R10 | med | Agents and Rules have no actual check, yet `Last audited` is stamped for them; `brain-audit`/`doctor-plus` are named as delegates with no ownership row. | **ACCEPTED.** `rot.md` initializes every layer to `unknown` except Skills (genuinely audited 2026-09-12). Each layer gets a concrete check or an explicit "no check yet." Dates advance only after that layer's check runs. |

---

### Task 1: Snapshot and freeze the current state

**Files:**
- Create: `~/.claude/skills-archive/pre-canonical-2026-09-12.tgz`
- Create: `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/2026-09-12-pre-canonical-inventory.txt`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: nothing.
- Produces: the rollback path for Tasks 2–4, and `pre-canonical-inventory.txt`, the baseline later tasks diff against.

**Note on undo, corrected after round 1:** there are now **two** undo paths. The tarball below covers the un-versioned folders (`~/.agents/skills`, `~/.codex/skills`). For `~/.claude/skills` the real undo is git — `3ab4467` already committed and pushed the 99 deletions, so `git -C ~/.claude/skills revert 3ab4467` restores them on both machines. The `skills-archive/` folder is *not* in that repo and does not reach Windows.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the inventory**

{

  find ~/.claude/skills -maxdepth 1 -type l -exec basename {} \; | sort
  echo "--- support dirs in claude skills (NO SKILL.md, DO NOT DELETE) ---"
  for d in ~/.claude/skills/*/; do [ -f "$d/SKILL.md" ] || basename "$d"; done | sort

wc -l < ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/2026-09-12-pre-canonical-inventory.txt
```

Expected: roughly 520–540 lines. **Read the "support dirs" section** — it must list `_shared`. That list is the do-not-delete set for every later task.

- [ ] **Step 2: Take the tarball**

```bash

  -C ~ .claude/skills .codex/skills .agents/skills

```

Expected: a non-zero-size file. `tar` may print `Removing leading '/'` — harmless.

- [ ] **Step 3: Verify the tarball actually restores**

```bash

tar xzf ~/.claude/skills-archive/pre-canonical-2026-09-12.tgz -C /tmp/tartest

Expected: `61`, `306`, `_shared OK`. If any is wrong, STOP — the snapshot is not a valid undo and no later task may run.

- [ ] **Step 4: Record both rollback paths**

cat >> ~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/2026-09-12-pre-canonical-inventory.txt <<'EOF'

=== ROLLBACK ===

# Canonical repo (undoes anything committed to erash11/claude-skills):

git -C ~/.claude/skills revert <sha>    # reaches Windows on next dev-sync

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

git add docs/audits/2026-09-12-pre-canonical-inventory.txt docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-12-harness-agnostic-aios.md

---

### Task 2: Prune the stale pool mirror

**Files:**
- Modify: `~/.agents/skills/` (move stale dirs out)
- Create: `~/.agents/skills-archive/2026-09-12/`
- Create: `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/2026-09-12-pool-prune.txt`

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: an `~/.agents/skills/` free of skills the audit already cut. Task 7 (Pi) reads this directly.

**Why this task exists:** yesterday's audit cut `~/.claude/skills/` and committed it. It never touched `~/.agents/skills/`, where 98 of the 99 archived names still live. Pi discovers that folder natively, so the token win evaporates the moment Pi runs.

The pool has a **mixed role**: a view onto Eric's own skills *and* an install target for third-party skills (`npx skills add` — see the `vendored-skill-install` memory). This task prunes **only** the 98 that exactly match yesterday's archive list. It does not touch the other 150, which may be third-party installs other harnesses depend on. Those are `aios-audit`'s problem, with a human reading the proposal.

comm -12 <(ls ~/.claude/skills-archive/2026-09-12 | sort) <(ls ~/.agents/skills | sort) \

find ~/.claude/skills -maxdepth 1 -type l -exec readlink {} \; \

### Task 3: Harden the sync writers — before anything moves

**Files:**
- Modify: `~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh`

- Create: `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/docs/audits/2026-09-12-sync-hardening.md`

**Interfaces:**

- Produces: a sync script safe to run at any point during Tasks 4–7. **Nothing in Task 4 may run until this task's Step 6 passes.**

**Why this task comes before the move.** Round 1 put the relink first and this second. Codex caught that as R1, a data-loss defect. Today `sync-to-codex.sh` does:

```bash

```bash

echo "=== ps1 ==="

- [ ] **Step 2: Rewrite the bash script**

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sync-to-codex.sh -- rebuild the Codex and agent-pool VIEWS from the canonical
# repo at ~/.claude/skills.
#
# CANONICAL: ~/.claude/skills   (git repo erash11/claude-skills, real dirs only)
# VIEWS:     ~/.agents/skills   (Pi, Cowork)
#            ~/.codex/skills    (Codex)
#
# Views are generated. Never author a skill in a view; it will be overwritten.
# On macOS a view entry is a symlink; on Windows the .ps1 twin copies instead.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
SHARED=(new-project startup dev-sync closeout session-handoff humanizer articulation-skill)
MODE="${SYNC_MODE:-link}"     # link | copy
DRY="${DRY_RUN:-0}"

fail=0
for s in "${SHARED[@]}"; do
  # R1 GUARD: the canonical source must be a real directory, never a link.
  # If it is a link, a previous migration inverted the direction and a
  # delete-then-copy would destroy the real data. Refuse the whole run.
  if [ -L "$SRC/$s" ]; then
    echo "FATAL $SRC/$s is a symlink. Canonical must be a real directory." >&2
    echo "      Refusing to sync; this would delete the link target." >&2
    fail=1
  fi
done
if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "No changes made." >&2
  exit 2
fi

for dst in "$HOME/.agents/skills" "$HOME/.codex/skills"; do
  mkdir -p "$dst"
  for s in "${SHARED[@]}"; do
    if [ ! -d "$SRC/$s" ]; then
      echo "skip $s (not in $SRC)"
      continue
    fi
    if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
      echo "would sync $s -> $dst ($MODE)"
      continue
    fi
    # Safe now: $SRC/$s is proven real, so removing the view cannot touch it.
    rm -rf "$dst/$s"
    if [ "$MODE" = "link" ]; then
      ln -s "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    else
      cp -R "$SRC/$s" "$dst/$s"
    fi
    echo "synced $s -> $dst ($MODE)"
  done
done

if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
  echo "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=0 to apply)"
fi
exit 0
```

Edit `~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.ps1`. Before its copy loop, add:

    Write-Error "FATAL $p is a link. Canonical must be a real directory. Refusing to sync."

}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Invert outward symlinks so ~/.claude/skills holds real directories only.
#   before: ~/.claude/skills/X -> ~/.agents/skills/X   (real content outside git)
#   after:  ~/.claude/skills/X is real; ~/.agents/skills/X -> it
# Idempotent. DRY_RUN=1 by default.
set -euo pipefail

SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
POOL="$HOME/.agents/skills"
DRY="${DRY_RUN:-1}"
moved=0; skipped=0

for link in "$SRC"/*; do
  name="$(basename "$link")"
  case "$name" in .*) continue ;; esac
  if [ ! -L "$link" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  target="$(cd "$(dirname "$link")" && readlink "$link")"
  abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$link")" && cd "$(dirname "$target")" 2>/dev/null && pwd)/$(basename "$target")"
  if [ ! -d "$abs" ]; then
    echo "DANGLING $name -> $target (left alone)"
    skipped=$((skipped+1))
    continue
  fi
  if [ ! -f "$abs/SKILL.md" ]; then
    echo "NO-SKILL  $name -> $target (support dir, left alone)"
    skipped=$((skipped+1))
    continue
  fi
  echo "INVERT    $name  ($abs -> $SRC/$name, link back at pool)"
  if [ "$DRY" = "0" ]; then
    rm "$link"
    mv "$abs" "$SRC/$name"
    ln -s "$SRC/$name" "$abs"
  fi
  moved=$((moved+1))
done

echo
echo "inverted: $moved   skipped: $skipped"
echo "symlinks left in canonical: $(find "$SRC" -maxdepth 1 -type l | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$DRY" = "1" ]; then
  echo "(DRY RUN - set DRY_RUN=0 to apply)"
fi
exit 0
```

**The portable frontmatter contract** (a superset — Codex ignores keys it does not know, Claude Code ignores `metadata`):

```yaml
---
name: skill-name                       # REQUIRED. Must equal the directory name.
                                       # TitleCase is allowed (CreateSkill, Harvest).
description: >-                        # REQUIRED. <=1024 chars. Must contain BOTH:
  <what it does, one sentence>.        #   (a) a positive clause: "Use when ..." with
  Use when <literal trigger phrases>.  #       literal phrases the user would type
  Do not use when <negative>.          #   (b) a negative clause: "Do not use ..." /
                                       #       "NOT FOR ..." - Codex needs this to
                                       #       avoid over-firing
metadata:
  short-description: <one short line>  # optional, Codex-only, Claude ignores
argument-hint: "[...]"                 # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Grep        # optional, Claude-only, Codex ignores
---
```

Claude Code triggers on literal phrases; Codex leans on the negative clause. A description with only one half fires reliably in one harness and badly in the other. **Naming is settled here (R7):** the rule is `name` equals the directory name. TitleCase is legal — `CreateSkill` and `Harvest` already ship that way and renaming them would break every cross-reference.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check every skill in the canonical repo against the portable frontmatter
contract. Exit 0 = all pass, 1 = failures, 2 = empty/missing inventory.
stdlib only (PEP 668 machine). Parses the flat YAML subset we actually use."""
import os, re, sys, glob

CANON = os.path.expanduser("~/.claude/skills")
ALLOWED = {"name", "description", "metadata", "argument-hint", "allowed-tools",
           "model", "disable-model-invocation", "license", "version", "author"}
POSITIVE = ("use when", "use for", "use this skill when", "invoke when")
NEGATIVE = ("do not use", "don't use", "not for", "never use")

def frontmatter(text):
    if not text.startswith("---"):
        return None
    end = text.find("\n---", 3)
    return None if end == -1 else text[4:end]

def top_keys(fm):
    return [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"(?m)^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*)\s*:", fm)]

def scalar(fm, key):
    """Read a flat scalar, including >- and | block styles."""
    m = re.search(rf"(?ms)^{re.escape(key)}\s*:[ \t]*(.*?)(?=^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*\s*:|\Z)", fm)
    if not m:
        return ""
    raw = m.group(1)
    raw = re.sub(r"^[>|][-+]?\s*\n", "", raw)          # strip a block indicator
    val = " ".join(l.strip() for l in raw.splitlines() if l.strip())
    return val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")

def check(path):
    name = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(path))
    problems = []
    fm = frontmatter(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read())
    if fm is None:
        return name, ["no YAML frontmatter"]
    keys = top_keys(fm)
    declared = scalar(fm, "name")
    if "name" not in keys:
        problems.append("missing 'name'")
    elif declared != name:
        problems.append(f"name '{declared}' != directory '{name}'")
    desc = scalar(fm, "description")
    if not desc:
        problems.append("missing 'description'")
    else:
        low = desc.lower()
        if len(desc) > 1024:
            problems.append(f"description {len(desc)} chars (>1024)")
        pos = next((p for p in POSITIVE if p in low), None)
        neg = next((n for n in NEGATIVE if n in low), None)
        if not pos:
            problems.append("no positive clause ('Use when ...') - Claude will not trigger")
        if not neg:
            problems.append("no negative clause ('Do not use ...') - Codex over-fires")
        # R7: the two clauses must be distinct text, not one phrase counted twice.
        if pos and neg and low.find(pos) == low.find(neg):
            problems.append("positive and negative clauses overlap")
    for k in keys:
        if k not in ALLOWED:
            problems.append(f"unknown frontmatter key '{k}'")
    return name, problems

def main():
    if not os.path.isdir(CANON):
        print(f"FATAL canonical dir missing: {CANON}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(CANON, "*", "SKILL.md")))
    if not paths:
        print(f"FATAL no SKILL.md found under {CANON} - refusing to report success",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    failed = 0
    for p in paths:
        name, probs = check(p)
        if probs:
            failed += 1
            print(f"FAIL {name}")
            for x in probs:
                print(f"       - {x}")
    print(f"\nchecked {len(paths)} skills, {failed} failing, {len(paths)-failed} portable")
    return 1 if failed else 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Machine-readable AIOS metrics. stdlib only. Prints key=value lines only."""
import os, re, glob, subprocess, collections, datetime, sys

H = os.path.expanduser("~")
CANON = f"{H}/.claude/skills"
POOL = f"{H}/.agents/skills"
CODEX = f"{H}/.codex/skills"
BUILTIN = {'exit','clear','compact','rename','color','login','logout','plugin',
'doctor','help','model','config','resume','cost','status','init','agents','mcp',
'hooks','memory','review','vim','terminal-setup','install-github-app','add-dir',
'bug','release-notes','pr-comments','ide','permissions','statusline',
'output-style','todos','export','privacy-settings','upgrade','fast','artifacts',
'tasks','loop','context','usage','rewind','sandbox','feedback','worktrees',
'skills','reload-skills','reload-plugins','bashes','keybindings','theme'}

def skills_in(root):
    """Count distinct skills under root, deduped by real path (R6).
    glob traverses symlinked dirs, so a link and its target counted twice."""
    seen = set()
    for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*")):
        s = os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md")
        if os.path.isfile(s):
            seen.add(os.path.realpath(s))
    return len(seen)

def names_in(root):
    return {os.path.basename(d) for d in glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "*"))
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d, "SKILL.md"))}

def usage():
    c = collections.Counter()
    for f in glob.glob(f"{H}/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl", recursive=True):
        try:
            for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"):
                if 'Skill' not in line and 'command-name' not in line:
                    continue
                for m in re.finditer(
                        r'"name"\s*:\s*"Skill"\s*,\s*"input"\s*:\s*\{[^}]*?"skill"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
                for m in re.finditer(r'<command-name>/([a-zA-Z0-9:_-]+)</command-name>', line):
                    c[m.group(1)] += 1
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {k: v for k, v in c.items()
            if k.split(':')[-1] not in BUILTIN and k not in BUILTIN}

def roster_tokens():
    """Frontmatter chars / 4 - what the roster costs per session."""
    total = 0
    for p in glob.glob(f"{CANON}/*/SKILL.md"):
        try:
            t = open(p, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore").read()
            end = t.find("\n---", 3)
            if t.startswith("---") and end != -1:
                total += len(t[4:end])
